stem: Meera notes that Diwali, which follows a luni-solar calendar, fell on a different Gregorian date this year compared to last year, while the solar harvest festival Makar Sankranti fell on almost the same date both years. Why does Makar Sankranti stay on nearly the same Gregorian date?

options.text: It is decided by the full Moon each year
It follows the solar cycle, which matches the Gregorian calendar closely
An extra month is added to the calendar every few years
All festivals fall on fixed Gregorian dates every year

teacher.key_rationale: Solar (sidereal) festivals follow the solar cycle, which the Gregorian calendar also tracks, so their dates stay nearly fixed; lunar-phase tracking (A) causes shifting, intercalation (C) only limits drift in luni-solar systems, and D is false because lunar festivals do shift.
